_comment: Nemotron-3 Super's multi-token-prediction head (DeepSeek-V3-style `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`). It ships inside its target's HF checkpoint (`checkpoint_of`), so it has no configs of its own: under `spec/mtp` it compiles on every selected `nemotron-h-latent` config that declares its layers (`mtp_num_hidden_layers` above zero, the source its `num_hidden_layers` replaces from), that config verbatim. A hybrid target's config also carries the TARGET's block schedule — `hybrid_override_pattern` (88 layers) and `num_hidden_layers`, both present, and config aliases fill absent keys only — so this dir's per-stem `.overrides.json` restores the head's own: its schedule from the checkpoint's `mtp_hybrid_override_pattern` (`*E`, an attention layer then a LatentMoE one — the target's mix in miniature), its layer count as `num_hidden_layers` (a schedule's length must equal a present count when the block sets derive), and the target's count preserved as `target_num_hidden_layers` (the head's KV pool is the target's, so its codec is decided at the target's layer count — the gemma4-assistant override carries its target's the same way). The OptiQ conversion publishes the head's tensors in a sidecar file the checkpoint's config names (`mtp_file`, `optiq/mtp.safetensors`) under this arch's `checkpoint_prefix` (`mtp.*`, nvidia's naming); the worker loads them from there and lends them under the bare names the head binds (`layers.0.*`, `layers.1.*`; hence the empty decoder prefix). No repo publishes it apart, so it names no drafter repo. It has no embed_tokens / lm_head of its own: the loader lends it the target's — and unlike Qwen3.5's it drafts over the FULL vocabulary (131072 rows: the lm_head read is no smaller a fraction of this head's step than of the target's own, so a prefix slice would only cost it drafts it cannot make). The latent expert path is the target's (`fc1_latent_proj` down, relu2 experts on the latent, `fc2_latent_proj` back up, full-width shared expert) with the nemotron-h declarations verbatim (`mixer` renames, `layer_norm_epsilon`, `scale_dtype: bf16`). It drafts `spec_drafts` tokens a step while the step holds at most `spec_max_seqs` sequences (two, the qwen head's measured gate: a verify step of two runs six rows, within the eight-row verify-sized bucket). Its KV is its own (one GQA layer, 32 query heads over 2 KV heads of 128 — the target's geometry), a pool mirroring the target's blocks.
